characters.continuity: The Silmarillion / The Lord of the Rings (Tolkien Legendarium)
characters.summary: Celebrimbor is the greatest Elvensmith of the Second Age in Eregion, renowned for crafting the Rings of Power with Sauron's guidance. In combat, he relies on elven weaponry, craftsmanship, and leadership rather than overt magical warfare.
weaknesses: Vulnerability to psychological manipulation and deception by Sauron
limitations: Over-reliance on his own craft, leaving him susceptible to Sauron's deceit regarding the Rings.

sources.supports: Role as Elvensmith, creation of the Rings of Power, and fate during the War of the Elves and Sauron.

feats.claim: Forged the Three Rings of the Elves independently of Sauron's direct corruption.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Rings of Power and the Third Age

notableResults.citation: The Silmarillion - The War of the Elves and Sauron
notableResults.note: Defended Eregion but was eventually captured and killed when Sauron overran the realm.

unknowns: Exact combat capabilities and martial feats prior to the siege of Eregion are sparsely detailed.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings / The Silmarillion (Tolkien Legendarium)
characters.summary: Círdan is one of the oldest and wisest Elves remaining in Middle-earth, Lord of the Havens of Mithlond. He is a master shipbuilder and counselor rather than a frontline combatant, though possessed of great foresight.
weaknesses: Not primarily focused on martial prowess or offensive combat
limitations: Prefers stewardship and escape routes over direct conquest.

sources.supports: Círdan's identity as shipbuilder, bearer of Narya initially, and longevity.

feats.claim: Fought in the Last Alliance of Elves and Men against Sauron.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion / The Fellowship of the Ring

notableResults.citation: The Silmarillion - War of the Last Alliance
notableResults.note: Participated in the successful siege of Barad-dûr alongside Gil-galad and Elendil.

conditional.ability: Possession and use of Narya, the Ring of Fire
conditional.dependsOn: Holding the ring before gifting it to Gandalf

unknowns: Exact details of his personal combat style during the First and Second Ages.

characters.continuity: The Hobbit / The Lord of the Rings (Tolkien Legendarium)
characters.summary: Dáin II Ironfoot is a formidable Dwarf king of Durin's Folk, wielding a heavy red axe with devastating skill. He is heavily armored and possesses legendary endurance and physical strength.

mechanisms: Heavy dwarven mail and iron boots

weaknesses: Vulnerable to flanking and overwhelming numbers despite heavy armor
limitations: Limited mobility due to heavy armor and advanced age in later years.

sources.supports: Dáin's role in the Battle of the Five Armies, combat prowess with an axe, and death at Dale.

feats.claim: Slew Azog the Defiler outside the gates of Moria as a young dwarf.
Fought fiercely at the Battle of the Five Armies, cutting down numerous goblins and orcs.

notableResults.note: Defeated Azog in single combat during the War of the Dwarves and Orcs.

notableResults.citation: The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A
notableResults.note: Slain defending the body of King Brand before the gates of Erebor during the War of the Ring.

unknowns: Exact age-related decline during the War of the Ring.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings (Tolkien Legendarium)
characters.summary: Denethor II is the Ruling Steward of Gondor, a proud, stern leader of great willpower and ancient Númenórean blood. He wields a longsword and has formidable mental fortitude, though broken psychologically by despair and the Palantír.
weaknesses: Severe psychological despair and manipulation via the Anorien Palantír
limitations: Prone to fatalistic despair when faced with overwhelming odds.

sources.supports: Denethor's role as Steward, use of the Palantír, and death in Minas Tirith.

feats.claim: Maintained resistance against Sauron's mental domination through the palantír for years before breaking.
feats.citation: The Return of the King, The Pyre of Denethor

notableResults.note: Mentally broken by Sauron's overwhelming displays via the Palantír, leading to suicide.

unknowns: Active combat feats in field battles during his earlier years as commander.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings (Tolkien Legendarium)
characters.summary: Durin's Bane is a Balrog of Morgoth, an ancient Maia spirit of fire and shadow. It wields a fiery whip and a broad-bladed sword of black flame, possessing immense physical strength, heat, and destructive magic.

techniques: Aura of intense heat and darkness

mechanisms: Warping aura of fire and shadow

weaknesses: Vulnerable to exceptionally powerful divine or magical forces (such as Gandalf's power)
limitations: Bound to physical form in Middle-earth; susceptible to fatal exhaustion in prolonged magical combat.

sources.supports: Balrog attributes, weapon usage, status as a Maia, and encounter in Moria.

feats.claim: Drove the Dwarves out of Khazad-dûm, killing King Náin I and King Thrór's grandfather.
feats.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring / Appendices

feats.claim: Fought Gandalf the Grey across days from the depths of Moria to the peak of Zirakzigil.
feats.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring, The Bridge of Khazad-dûm and The White Rider

notableResults.citation: The Two Towers, The White Rider
notableResults.note: Slain by Gandalf on Zirakzigil after an exhaustive multi-day battle.

campaignTags.claim: Surrounded by fire, smoke, and wields a fiery whip.
Generates and controls intense magical fire and heat.
Wields a fiery whip and a sword of flame.

unknowns: Whether Balrogs possess true powered flight or merely glide/inspire terror with shadow.

characters.continuity: The Hobbit / The Lord of the Rings (Tolkien Legendarium)
characters.summary: Dwalin is a stout Dwarf of Thorin's company, a veteran warrior skilled with a battleaxe, hammer, and sword. He is heavily armored and fights with fierce frontline aggression.
weaknesses: Standard physical vulnerabilities of mortal dwarves
limitations: Limited range; relies entirely on close-quarters melee combat.

sources.supports: Dwalin's role in Thorin's company and weapon preferences.

feats.claim: Survived numerous skirmishes during the quest of Erebor, including battles with trolls, goblins, and wargs.
Fought in the Battle of the Five Armies.

notableResults.note: Successfully fought off goblins in the goblin tunnels alongside his companions.

unknowns: Specific individual feats during the War of the Ring due to old age.

characters.summary: Eärendil the Mariner is a half-elven hero who sailed the skies of Arda bearing the Silmaril. He possesses celestial navigation mastery, divine blessing, and fights aboard his flying ship Vingilot.
weaknesses: Dependent on his ship and the light of the Silmaril for extraordinary cosmic power
limitations: Bound to the skies of the upper atmosphere after his transformation.

sources.supports: Eärendil's lineage, voyage with the Silmaril, and defeat of Ancalagon the Black.

feats.claim: Slew the great dragon Ancalagon the Black in aerial combat during the War of Wrath.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion, Of the Voyage of Eärendil and the War of Wrath

notableResults.note: Defeated the greatest of Morgoth's dragons in the skies above Thangorodrim with the help of the great eagles.

conditional.dependsOn: The flying ship Vingilot and the Silmaril

campaignTags.claim: Sails the sky aboard the flying ship Vingilot.

unknowns: Exact mechanics of how Vingilot achieves sustained celestial flight.

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings / The Silmarillion (Tolkien Legendarium)
characters.summary: Elendil the Tall is the High King of Arnor and Gondor, a mighty Númenórean warrior of immense stature and physical strength. He wields the legendary sword Narsil and wears peerless plate armor.
weaknesses: Vulnerable to extreme heat and overwhelming magical or physical trauma
limitations: Mortal limits despite exceptional Númenórean lifespan and physique.

sources.supports: Elendil's role as High King, wielding of Narsil, and death in combat against Sauron.

feats.claim: Led the armies of Men alongside Gil-galad in the Last Alliance against Sauron.
feats.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring, Council of Elrond

notableResults.citation: The Silmarillion / The Fellowship of the Ring
notableResults.note: Slain in single combat on the slopes of Orodruin alongside Gil-galad, though Sauron was simultaneously overthrown.

campaignTags.claim: Noted for exceptional height and stature as a high-ranking Númenórean.

unknowns: Exact details of his swordplay techniques apart from wielding Narsil.
